subject: Creating new data under model (for GoF) results in infinite loop?

messages.author: 1ce64fad997d9303
messages.subject: Creating new data under model (for GoF) results in infinite loop?
parts:
Hi all,

PROBLEM DESCRIPTION:

I have a fairly straightforward N-mix model, and I'm trying to add  a goodness-of-fit test using posterior predictive distributions of chi2 discrepancy (as detailed in AHM 6.8). However, I'm having an issue creating a new data set under the model (for species b, visit v):

 C.sim[b,v] ~ dbin( p[year_id[v],b], N[site_id[v], year_id[v], b] )

Nimble is giving me the following warnings, consecutively/simultaneously, for some (but not all!) values of C.sim[b,v] and N[s,t,b], which seem to create an infinite loop such that the model never fits:

"warning: problem initializing stochastic node C.sim[1, 1]: logProb is -Inf."

"Warning: slice sampler reached maximum number of contractions for 'N[1, 1, 1]'. Current parameter value is 59."

I thought it might just be that I need initial values for C.sim, since occasionally that happened with N and I learned on this listserv that could be fixed by adding an init for lambda. But, there's not quite a lambda equivalent for C.sim, and adding an init for C.sim itself has not helped:

inits <- list(
  C.sim = array(1, dim =c(
    n.data$nspecies,
    n.data$nvisits)),
  lambda = array(1, dim =c(
    n.data$nyears,
    n.data$nspecies)),
  N = Nst,
  p = array(0.3, dim = c(
    n.data$nyears,
    n.data$nspecies))
)

Is there a way to solve this? Thanks for any advice! Full code below my name.

Best,
Gates


ALL CODE FOR REFERENCE:

# ---- Specifying the model ----

n.code <- nimbleCode( {
 
  # PRIORS
  for(b in 1:nspecies){
    for(t in 1:nyears){
     
      # Expected count
      lambda[t,b] ~ dgamma(0.001, 0.001)
      # Detection probability
      p[t,b] ~ dunif(0,1)
     
    }
  }
 
 
  # LIKELIHOOD
  # Ecological model
  for(b in 1:nspecies){
    for(t in 1:nyears){
      for(s in 1:nsites) {
       
        # Latent site abundance
        N[s,t,b] ~ dpois(lambda[t,b])
       
      }
    }
  }
 
  # Observation model
  # Using nested indexing because there is a lot of missing data!
  for(b in 1:nspecies){
    for(v in 1:nvisits){
     
      # Observed count
      C[b,v] ~ dbin( p[year_id[v],b], N[site_id[v], year_id[v], b] )
     
    }
  }
 
 
  # GOODNESS-OF-FIT
  for(b in 1:nspecies){
    for(v in 1:nvisits){
      # # Commenting out parts that require C.sim
      # # Create new data set under model
      C.sim[b,v] ~ dbin( p[year_id[v],b], N[site_id[v], year_id[v], b] )
      # # Expected datum
      e.count[b,v] <- N[site_id[v], year_id[v], b] * p[year_id[v],b]
      # # Chi-square discrepancy for the actual data
      chi2.actual[b,v] <- pow((C[b,v]-e.count[b,v]),2) / (e.count[b,v]+0.001)
      # # Chi-square discrepancy for the simulated ('perfect') data
      # chi2.sim[b,v] <- pow((C.sim[b,v]-e.count[b,v]),2) / (e.count[b,v]+0.001)
      # # Add small value e to denominator to avoid division by zero
    }
  }

  # # Add up individual chi2 values for overall fit statistic
  fit.actual <- sum(chi2.actual[1:nspecies,1:nvisits]) # Fit statistic for actual data set
  # fit.sim <- sum(chi2.sim[1:nspecies,1:nvisits]) # Fit statistic for a fitting model
  # c.hat <- fit.actual / fit.sim # c-hat estimate
  # bpv <- step(fit.sim-fit.actual) # Bayesian p-value
 
})


# ---- Defining settings for the model and MCMC ----

inits <- list(
  C.sim = array(1, dim =c(
    n.data$nspecies,
    n.data$nvisits)),
  lambda = array(1, dim =c(
    n.data$nyears,
    n.data$nspecies)),
  N = Nst, # created elsewhere
  p = array(0.3, dim = c(
    n.data$nyears,
    n.data$nspecies))
)

# Parameters monitored
# params <- c("lambda", "p", "fit.actual", "fit.sim", "c.hat", "bpv")
params <- c("lambda", "p")

# MCMC settings
ni <- 25000   ;   nt <- 20   ;   nb <- 5000   ;   nc <- 3


# ---- Prepping and running the MCMC ----

hcm_mod <- nimbleModel(n.code, constants = n.data,
                       check = F, calculate = F)

hcm_mcmc <- buildMCMC(hcm_mod, monitors = params)

hcm_comp0 <- compileNimble(hcm_mod)

hcm_comp <- compileNimble(hcm_mcmc, project = hcm_mod)

hcm_samples <- runMCMC(
  hcm_comp,
  thin = nt,
  nburnin = nb,
  niter = ni,
  nchains = nc,
  inits = inits)
